sections.title: Stems and saline habitat
sections.text: Common glasswort is a small annual halophyte of salt marshes and mudflats. It reaches about 10–40 cm. Its upright stems are fleshy and jointed; the leaves are reduced to tiny, nearly invisible scales.

sections.title: Flowers and seeds
sections.text: Minute flowers are embedded in the upper stem segments; seeds develop in small fruits. The stems often turn red or purple in autumn. The plate accurately shows the branched habit, fleshy joints and inconspicuous flowers.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: Young shoots of glassworts are eaten as a vegetable, raw or cooked, and taste salty. Identification matters because the common name “glasswort” covers several species; plants from polluted sites should not be harvested.
